entries.supportPhrase: In English, convert the address to hex
entries.conditionalHypothesis: For a 20-byte address, EIP-55 casing is reproducibly derived by Keccak-256 of its lowercase hex digits, not SHA3-256 or the mixed-case input.
entries.preconditions: Exactly 20 address bytes; hash of lowercase hexadecimal ASCII; compare nibble case only where the character is alphabetic.
entries.positiveControl: Re-encode each pinned positive test vector and obtain exactly the documented mixed-case output.
entries.adversarialControl: Flip one alphabetic checksum nibble in each selected vector and check rejection under a strict checksum validator; measure accidental collision acceptance rather than assuming every changed address is rejected.
entries.falsificationCriterion: An independent, byte-for-byte implementation and a pinned reference vector yield different casing for the same input under identical assumptions.
requiredIndependentEvidence: Selected mutation corpus and collision notes
uncertainties: Do not equate optional user-interface acceptance of lowercase addresses with failure of the canonical checksum encoder.

entries.conditionalHypothesis: For the ERC-191 0x00 intended-validator format, changing only the validator-address domain changes the signed preimage and should invalidate a signature produced for the original validator under correct verification.
entries.preconditions: Use the 0x19+0x00 format, identical signer/key/payload and the exact intended-validator address; control ECDSA digest encoding.
entries.positiveControl: Recover the signing address with an independently computed version-0 preimage for the intended validator.
entries.adversarialControl: Use the same signature and payload for a different intended validator; check that the recovered signer no longer matches (within the pinned test fixtures).
entries.falsificationCriterion: The same signature is accepted for different validator domains by an implementation claiming proper validator binding, without an explicit allowed cross-domain policy.
requiredIndependentEvidence: Pinned verifier or contract bytecode with test fixtures
uncertainties: No claim that a signature scheme is globally replay-proof without chain-id, nonce, expiry and other relevant domains.

entries.supportPhrase: A diamond calls functions from its facets using
entries.conditionalHypothesis: With a pinned diamond implementation, calls to an installed facet selector should execute using diamond storage, and facet-cut changes should be observable in the prescribed DiamondCut event when applied.
entries.preconditions: Known facet selector mapping, deployed diamond/facet code hashes, delegatecall semantics and the particular implementation's upgrade authorization policy.
entries.positiveControl: Install a known facet using an authorized cut, inspect selector mapping and emitted event, and verify a deliberate state update in diamond storage.
entries.adversarialControl: Attempt an unauthorized cut and a selector replacement/clash; verify exact access policy, event consistency and state isolation under the chosen implementation.
entries.falsificationCriterion: The implementation reports a successful facet cut with an inconsistent selector mapping or without a required DiamondCut event, or violates its declared authorization policy.
requiredIndependentEvidence: Authenticated transaction receipts and event logs
uncertainties: The ERC does not by itself prove a specific admin model or security of arbitrary facet code.

entries.conditionalHypothesis: The published ERC-7201 formula produces deterministic namespace storage roots under a fixed namespace ID, and a pinned compiler-annotated struct should agree with that computation.
entries.preconditions: Treat the ID as the specified UTF-8 byte sequence; evaluate keccak256(abi.encode(uint256(keccak256(bytes(id))) - 1)) & ~bytes32(uint256(0xff)); keep 256-bit arithmetic fixed.
entries.positiveControl: Compute the namespace slot using two independent implementations and compare with a compiler/AST NatSpec annotation in a pinned example.
entries.adversarialControl: Vary namespace ID or formula ordering, assert independently computed address differs for selected test vectors, and test collision/alias behavior for deliberate misannotation.
entries.falsificationCriterion: Two independent evaluations of the exact formula disagree on the same namespace input or a pinned claimed-implementation uses a different root than its declared ID.
requiredIndependentEvidence: Pinned exact formula and reference vectors
Solidity AST annotation and storage-layout sample
uncertainties: Different IDs are not mathematically guaranteed collision-free; the test only covers specified identifiers.

entries.conditionalHypothesis: An ERC-600 wallet following the described hierarchy should serialize a hardened BIP32 path whose purpose, subpurpose and EIP indices match the documented convention.
entries.preconditions: Pin the external BIP32 derivation definition; parse apostrophes as hardened markers; use purpose=43 and subpurpose=60 from pinned source.
entries.positiveControl: Parse and derive a known seed for the documented path with two independently pinned BIP32 implementations.
entries.adversarialControl: Change hardened markers or purpose/subpurpose, and demonstrate differing derived public identifiers in controlled reference vectors.
entries.falsificationCriterion: A wallet claiming the exact ERC-600 path yields a different derivation from the agreed BIP32 reference for the same seed/index path.
requiredIndependentEvidence: Pinned BIP32/SLIP44 versions and test vectors
Independent path parser and reference implementation
Explicit seed-handling test hygiene, no real user secrets
uncertainties: Do not test with live mnemonic or private keys; do not presume every wallet accepts ERC-600.

entries.conditionalHypothesis: A parser claiming the documented WalletConnect URI syntax should preserve the version discriminator and accept/reject mandatory v1 or v2 parameters according to the pinned document.
entries.preconditions: Parse only the URI grammar under this versioned specification; separate URI decoding from network pairing; no remote bridge contacted.
entries.positiveControl: Parse pinned v1 and v2 sample URI strings and reproduce topic, version and required field set.
entries.adversarialControl: Remove one mandatory parameter or swap v1/v2 parameter sets; check bounded parser rejection and percent-encoding edge cases.
entries.falsificationCriterion: A claimed parser silently accepts an explicitly invalid/missing required field or interprets version-specific parameters as a different version under the exact claimed grammar.
uncertainties: No cryptographic pairing or bridge availability is implied by a syntactically valid URI.

entries.conditionalHypothesis: A pinned implementation claiming ERC-1387 attestation validation should distinguish valid Merkle inclusion plus attester authorization from a mutated path or invalid attester signature.
entries.preconditions: Pin an actual implementation, Merkle hash/encoding order, attester trust root, and the complete signed payload; the draft interface alone is insufficient.
entries.positiveControl: Submit a known valid attester-signed Merkle proof to a locally deployed verifier and record its return/receipt.
entries.adversarialControl: Mutate a sibling-path hash, attestation recipient or signature; verify that the selected implementation rejects the altered proof under the same policy.
entries.falsificationCriterion: The selected implementation accepts a tampered inclusion proof or unauthorized signer while claiming to enforce the pinned policy.
requiredIndependentEvidence: Pinned Merkle tree shape and hash rules
uncertainties: The provided historic interface is not a complete proof-system definition; human semantic review mandatory.

entries.conditionalHypothesis: For a concrete issuer-list contract implementing the draft model, only the designated list manager should be able to change issuer membership, subject to its documented role model.
entries.preconditions: Pin ownership/manager role definition and deployed implementation; distinguish attester issuer addresses from signing keys.
entries.positiveControl: An authorized manager adds a known issuer; querying the list reflects the expected membership and capacity.
entries.adversarialControl: An unauthorized caller attempts add/remove, and an issuer with wrong capacity attempts trust validation; verify rejection under the particular implementation policy.
entries.falsificationCriterion: An implementation claiming manager-only mutation permits an unrelated address to change list membership or accepts an unauthorized issuer under the tested configuration.
uncertainties: Historic draft comments alone do not verify that any current deployed implementation enforces this policy.

entries.supportPhrase: This EIP defines a data format for *package manifest* documents
entries.conditionalHypothesis: A versioned EthPM manifest conforming to the pinned v3 schema should validate its mandatory structure, content-addressed references and declared package version.
entries.preconditions: Pin the complete EthPM v3 document and its precise JSON/schema vocabulary; do not equate valid JSON with an authenticated package.
entries.positiveControl: Validate a pinned minimal manifest against a second independent parser/schema and resolve only controlled offline fixtures.
entries.adversarialControl: Mutate a declared package field, dependency or content hash; verify that strict schema or integrity checks reject the altered artifact.
entries.falsificationCriterion: An implementation claiming to enforce the pinned schema accepts an invalid mandatory field or material source digest mismatch under its documented validation scope.
requiredIndependentEvidence: Pinned schema version and mandatory-field definitions
Offline immutable package and content hashes
uncertainties: No blockchain contract interaction is implied by a manifest, and syntax validity is not supply-chain trust.

entries.supportPhrase: Transferring ownership adds the new owner
entries.conditionalHypothesis: In the documented multi-owner model, a permitted transfer may add the recipient to an ownership set without removing the previous owner, unlike ordinary single-owner transfer semantics.
entries.preconditions: Use the specific multi-owner contract and exact provider-fee rule; only compare equivalent defined operations, not generic ERC-721 behavior.
entries.positiveControl: Issue a MO-NFT, transfer to another eligible owner and inspect that both original and new owners remain listed under the protocol's rules.
entries.adversarialControl: Test duplicate-owner additions, archived-owner transfers and insufficient provider fee; examine whether behavior matches documented policies.
entries.falsificationCriterion: The pinned contract claims additive ownership but removes the prior owner after a transfer that should retain them.
requiredIndependentEvidence: Pinned MO-NFT source and owner-set ABI
Authentic before/after ownership and fee receipts
uncertainties: Do not claim universal ERC-721 interoperability solely from similarly named transferFrom.

entries.conditionalHypothesis: The diffusive transfer model proposes that positive transfers mint units for the recipient without decrementing sender balance, while keeping totalSupply at or below maxSupply.
entries.preconditions: Assume an eligible positive-quantity transfer, enough native fee, below maxSupply; distinguish these semantics from conservative ERC-20 transfers.
entries.positiveControl: Record positive before/after balances and supply under a reviewed implementation; verify minted amount, fee and maxSupply constraint.
entries.adversarialControl: Use maxSupply boundary, inadequate native fee and amount zero as controls; compare behavior against conventional ERC-20 and strict non-increasing supply only under explicitly shared roles.
entries.falsificationCriterion: An implementation claiming these transfer semantics decreases the sender balance or increases supply beyond maxSupply on an authorized positive transfer.
requiredIndependentEvidence: Pinned ERC-7837 implementation and supply math
Precise role equivalence before composition tests
uncertainties: A documentary contradiction with ERC-8098 supply monotonicity is only a conditional hypothesis, not demonstrated same-contract incompatibility.

entries.conditionalHypothesis: A deployed proxy claiming ERC-897 introspection should return a proxy type and implementation address consistent with its version-specific delegation behavior.
entries.preconditions: Pin the exact proxy implementation and type semantics; distinguish implementation() reporting from actual delegatecall target.
entries.positiveControl: Deploy a pinned proxy, call both introspection methods and verify the intended implementation by bytecode and delegation trace.
entries.adversarialControl: Exercise a fixed vs upgradeable instance and replace target if the type permits; check introspection stays in sync with dispatched code.
entries.falsificationCriterion: A purported compliant proxy advertises a target that does not correspond to its observed delegated runtime behavior under the documented type.
requiredIndependentEvidence: Pinned interface and concrete proxy bytecode
uncertainties: The two signatures alone do not establish the security of delegatecall or the upgrade authority.

entries.supportPhrase: The compatibility check `proxiable` prevents irreparable updates
entries.conditionalHypothesis: A pinned UUPS implementation should reject an upgrade to a logic contract with an incompatible proxiable identifier, while preserving proxy storage and its declared authorization policy.
entries.preconditions: Fix the actual proxy slot, proxiable UUID, upgrade authorization and implementation revision; do not infer safety from a UUID match alone.
entries.positiveControl: Upgrade to a compatible implementation under an authorized account and verify storage persistence and correct code dispatch.
entries.adversarialControl: Try an incompatible UUID, unauthorized upgrader or dangerous entrypoint invocation and verify rejection or documented limitation under the exact implementation.
entries.falsificationCriterion: An implementation claiming compatibility checks accepts an incompatible UUID or an unauthorized upgrade that its own policy forbids.
requiredIndependentEvidence: Exact proxiable UUID and storage-slot model
Negative upgrade/access/slot controls with local receipts
uncertainties: UUPS is an architectural pattern; this does not prove all proxy implementations immune to bricking or takeover.
